chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man vowed to walk to the House of Allah (Exalted is He). He said: 'Let him walk.' I said: But he will become weary. He said: 'Then when he becomes weary, he may ride.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone vows to walk to the Kaaba but gets tired?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in fulfilling vows (*nadhr*). It demonstrates the Shia juristic approach of balancing strict adherence to religious commitments with practical flexibility, allowing the vow-breaker to ride once physical exhaustion sets in rather than forcing them to continue to the point of harm.
